role: Trainee lawyer and lawyer (early legal career)
organization: Budapest Metropolitan Court (Fővárosi Bíróság) and international law practice
description: After graduating in law in 2004 he began at the Budapest Metropolitan Court and, after his bar examination, worked in international legal practice on corporate, commercial and competition matters. As a trainee lawyer he took part in pro bono legal help for people injured in the 2006 street protests. Details of this period come from encyclopaedic summaries rather than official records.

organization: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Hungary
description: Joined the foreign ministry after Fidesz won the 2010 parliamentary election.

organization: Permanent Representation of Hungary to the European Union, Brussels
description: Joined the permanent representation during Hungary's 2011 EU Council presidency, representing the government's positions in EU legislation, mainly on transport, energy, company and competition law.

role: Head-of-unit diplomat for relations with the European Parliament
description: Responsible for liaison between the Hungarian government and the European Parliament on legal, financial, budgetary, trade and development-policy files.

role: Head of the EU Legal Directorate
organization: Hungarian Development Bank (Magyar Fejlesztési Bank, MFB), state-owned
description: Headed the bank's EU legal directorate. The Hungarian-language encyclopaedia names the state development bank MFB; the English-language one names MBH Bank.

role: Chief executive officer (vezérigazgató); board member January 2021 – July 2022
organization: Diákhitel Központ Zrt. (Student Loan Centre), state-owned
description: Ran the state student-loan provider. His July 2024 European Parliament declaration lists a monthly income of 3,500,000 HUF as CEO and 400,000 HUF a month as board member. In 2024 he said he had been pressured in this role to favour people close to the government in tenders.
Declared monthly income of 400,000 HUF in his European Parliament declaration of private interests.
Declared monthly income of 3,000,000 HUF in his European Parliament declaration of private interests.

role: Member of the board of directors
organization: Magyar Közút Nonprofit Zrt. (state road operator)
description: Declared board fees of 1,875,000 HUF for August–December 2022, 1,475,800 HUF for 2023 and 1,794,000 HUF for January–February 2024. He announced his resignation from his state-company posts on 10 February 2024.
Declared monthly income of 1,500,000 HUF. He gave up the seat in February 2024 when he broke with the government.

role: Member of the board of directors
description: Declared monthly income of 1,100,000 HUF in his European Parliament declaration of private interests.

Joined the small, little-known Tisza party, founded in 2020, to be able to run in the June 2024 European Parliament election, and was elected its vice-president the same day. In March 2024 he had launched the Talpra Magyarok movement at a rally in Budapest.

Party leader since 22 July 2024, an unpaid position according to his declarations. Led the party to second place in the 2024 European Parliament election and to a two-thirds majority in the April 2026 parliamentary election.

role: Member of the European Parliament (EPP group); Vice-Chair of the Committee on Constitutional Affairs (AFCO)
description: Elected in June 2024 at the head of the Tisza list; sat in the Group of the European People's Party, was vice-chair of the Constitutional Affairs Committee and a member of the Agriculture Committee and of the delegations for relations with the United States and to the EU-UK Parliamentary Partnership Assembly. He gave up the seat after the April 2026 national election.

role: Member of the National Assembly (Országgyűlés) for Budapest's 3rd constituency
description: Elected in the constituency based in Budapest's 12th district on 12 April 2026; took his seat at the inaugural sitting on 9 May 2026.

Elected prime minister by the National Assembly on 9 May 2026 and sworn in the same day; his 17-member single-party cabinet (13 Tisza members and 4 independents) took office on 12–13 May 2026, with Anita Orbán and Bálint Ruff as deputy prime ministers.
